newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Main opposition United National party not to attend ceremony to commemorate its assassinated leader, former president Ranasinghe Premadasa.

Supreme Court grants leave to proceed in the funamdental rights action brought by Sirisena Cooray, a former minister in the Premadasa cabinet. Cooray, who was detained under the country's emergency laws, is being held in police custody on unspecified charges.
Air Force and ground troops of Operation Jaya Sikuru destroy Tamil rebel (LTTE) camps in Mankulam in the north, security sources said.
Jaya Sikuru troops who captured the LTTE stronghold of Puliyankulam, move on to Mankulam, further north, security sources say.

UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe tells his party members to either toe the line, or get out. Some party members are said to be at loggerheads with the leadership due to a UNP decision not to attend commomeration ceremonies for its late leader Ranasinghe Premadasa.
Police close down alleged LTTE "bank" in Colombo, which was used to distribute money to its cadres and take into custody large haul of Sri Lankan and Indian rupees, sources said.
